waveName: Wave 7 – Documentation, honest limitations & end-to-end consolidation

package.title: README limitations, feature docs and one e2e entry point
package.goal: The README describes exactly what MosaicPlan now does and does not do (requirement 18), and one command runs every end-to-end check.
steps: Document the raw-tile count semantics (a safe upper bound per identical cut shape), the dither trade-off, the cut minimum-width rule, the export/import with materials, and the PDF part and code-plan features.
e2e/run-e2e.cjs: keep the existing flow, then run every e2e/*.e2e.cjs in sequence with a summary. Exit non-zero on any failure.
tests/w7-i18n-ext.test.ts: assert that no two ext files override the same key, and that every ext file has key and placeholder parity across de, en and tr.
Run the full suite: typecheck, test, build, e2e, and `npm run android:sync`. Fix any small leftover integration seams. Record the results in the PR.
acceptance: `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` runs every package e2e script and passes.
README lists every limitation that remains and states which checks were device-unverified.
package.risk: Effort S-M. This package is last because it reflects the merged state; it must not change behaviour.

findings.title: Mixed tile sizes (req. 3) exist only as k×k cuts of the base stone, in sizes the user cannot choose, and are almost never used
findings.problem: Requirement 3 asks for different tile sizes in one project, with real positions and dimensions for each stone. The only mechanism is splitting a base cell into k×k pieces. The fine size is forced by (w−(k−1)g)/k, which is often not a size you can buy. Every fine piece is counted as cut from the large raw tile, because there is only one raw size per colour. The user therefore cannot plan 'fine stones from my 4 mm tiles'. The optimiser also almost never picks subdivision, even inside a marked face, so requirement 5 ('finer stones in faces, eyes, hair') is effectively not met.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/core1.out: sub-piece sizes are 2.00 mm (from 5/1), 3.50 mm (8/1), 3.25 mm (8/1.5) and 4.00 mm (10/2), always 'cut', yieldPerRaw 4. core2.out: SUB is used in 5 of 1004 face cells (0.5 %) at default detail and 14 (1.4 %) at detail 100 %. LINE wins because its penalty is 1.4·λ, against 2·λ for subdivision (mosaic.ts:336, :364). The raw size is set per colour only (src/core/stats.ts:73-81). The UI wording is in src/i18n/de.ts:140 ('tiles.mixedHint'). In shots/b2-eyes.png the only subdivided cell in view is at the nose bridge.
findings.proposal: Add 'Zonen mit eigenem Raster'. Zone {id, c0,c1,r0,r1 (base-grid index range), tileW, tileH, joint}. Zone span Lx = colX[c1−1]+colW[c1−1]−colX[c0], which is exact because it ends at stone outer edges. Inner grid = computeLayout({widthMm:Lx, heightMm:Ly, tileW, tileH, joint, edgeMode:'cut-both'}), offset by (colX[c0], rowY[r0]). The zone border lies in the base joint, so the gap between zone and base stones is exactly the base joint g. Base cells inside the zone get a new CellKind.ZONE with 0 pieces, so nothing is counted twice. The zone gets its own MosaicData from computeMosaic on the zone sub-image, with fixedPalette set to the project palette. If computeAxis returns rest>0, show the remainder rather than silently stretching. Offer exact-fit snapping. Example: base 10/2 mm with a 4/2 mm zone always fits, since 12n−2 = 2n·4+(2n−1)·2. Base 8/1 mm with a 4/1 mm zone fits whenever n is a multiple of 5. IDs 'Z1:A001' with absolute X/Y. Stats, CSV and PDF iterate the base grid plus zones. Raw material is chosen per (colour, tile size), so zone stones are uncut real tiles. splitAxis must not place section boundaries inside a zone span. The step-6 region tool creates zones from face or detail rectangles. Quick win first (S): replace the k choice with a 'target fine size' and offer only k where (w+g) = k·(w2+g). In that case, map the pieces to a material of size w2 and count them as uncut.
corrected:
Do the work in stages so that the stone-count invariants (each stone counted once, totals match geometry) stay testable at every step.

Stage 0 (S), honesty in the app (requirement 18):
- In StepGeometry.tsx:182, put an incomplete badge next to tiles.mixedHint. Reword it to: "Nur als 2×2/3×3-Teilung einer Rasterzelle; Zonen mit eigenem Raster fehlen noch."
- Next to the subdivide toggle in StepShapes.tsx, show the computed sub size (already computed there).
- If no material of that size exists in the material DB, add the warning "Teilsteine werden aus dem Grundstein geschnitten".

Stage 1 (M), real fine tiles for subdivided cells:
1. Replace the k segmented control with a "Feinstein-Größe" select. Offer only the sizes w2 for which (tileW+g) = k·(w2+g) with k in {2,3}; for k=4 or more the sample grid S=6 in mosaic.ts:127 would also need changing. Examples: 10/2 gives 4 mm (k=2), 5/1 gives 2 mm (k=2), 8/1 gives 2 mm (k=3). Store k and fineTileMm.
2. Add an optional fineMaterialId to PaletteColor. Extend makeRawSizeFn to (color, kind) and use the fine material for pieces of SUB cells. analyzeCut then reports needsCut=false and yieldPerRaw=1 automatically, because exactRaw holds (pieces.ts:244-246, 264).
3. Split ColorStat into per-(colour, raw size) rows so that packs, cost and the PDF/CSV material list are right for both tile sizes.
4. In the colour step, match each colour to the nearest material that has that size, using the same ΔE matching as today.
5. Tests:
   - Sum of pieces is unchanged by the switch.
   - Sub pieces are uncut exactly when the fine material size equals the sub size.
   - Full stones of the same colour still use the base material, so notFitting stays 0. Today it goes to 38 in the repro.

Stage 1b (S, tuning): inside face/detail regions with subdivision enabled, lower the SUB penalty in mosaic.ts:364 to at most LINE's 1.4·λ (or add a "Feine Steine in Gesichtern bevorzugen" toggle). Then check with the real-photo repro that face ΔE improves. At the default detail of 50 %, SUB is currently 0–1.7 % of face cells.

Stage 2 (L), zones with their own grid, as the auditor proposed:
1. Zone {id, c0, c1, r0, r1, tileW, tileH, joint}. Span Lx = colX[c1−1] + colW[c1−1] − colX[c0]. Inner layout from computeLayout(..., edgeMode 'cut-both'), offset by colX[c0] and rowY[r0]. Base cells inside a zone get CellKind.ZONE with 0 pieces.
2. Each zone has its own MosaicData and progress array, computed from the zone sub-image with the project palette as a fixed palette.
3. Offer exact-fit snapping:
   - 10/2 base with a 4/2 zone always fits.
   - 8/1 base with a 4/1 zone fits when n is a multiple of 5.
   - Otherwise, show the cut edge stones explicitly.
4. Changes to section splitting: do not forbid boundaries inside zones. Split a zone into sub-zones at each section boundary. Boundaries lie in base joints, so each sub-zone again has an exact span.
5. IDs use the form Z1:A001 with absolute X/Y.
6. Stats, CSV, PDF, render, Viewer hit-testing, StoneDialog edits and serialize must iterate base cells plus zones. Bump the format version and add a migration.
7. Add invariant tests:
   - No zone pieces overlap base pieces.
   - The total pieces in stats equal the sum over the base grid plus all zones.
   - Section counts add up to the total.
   - PDF counts equal the preview.

STAGE 1 (M): reuse the existing SUB stones, so every guarantee still holds.

(a) Fine-stone region ("Feinzone"):
- Add Region.type 'fine' next to face and detail (types.ts:84).
- In computeMosaic, after the analysis of each cell (mosaic.ts ~353-376): if the cell centre lies in a fine region and all subRects pass pieceCuttable, force bestKind=SUB and take the colours from gs.map(meanOf).
- If a piece is not cuttable, keep the normal choice and set Rec.FINER, so the cell is visibly marked as a recommendation.
- Draw these regions in the step-6 region editor with their own colour. The user then really gets fine stones in eyes, mouth and hair, instead of 1-2 % chance.

(b) Pick a target fine size instead of k:
- In StepShapes, list the k values that give an exact whole-mm size, fine = (w+g)/k − g, for example 10/2 gives 4 mm and 12/2 gives 5 mm.
- Show other k values honestly as "X,XX mm – wird aus dem Grundstein geschnitten".
- Allow k=4 only after changing the sample grid S to 12 for that path (needs S % k == 0).
- Hard-cap k at 4 because progress is a 16-bit mask per cell (edits.ts:128-134).

(c) Material for fine stones:
- Add PaletteColor.fineMaterialId.
- Change RawSizeFn to (color, pieceW, pieceH) and choose the fine material when the piece's bounding box exactly matches that material's size (within DIM_TOL). analyzeCut then returns needsCut=false and yield 1 without any other change. The CutCache key already contains the raw size.
- In computeStats (stats.ts:153-200), the PDF material table (pdf.ts:386-425) and the CSV, change perColor to one row per (colour, raw size). Each fine material then gets its own order line.
- Never relabel a piece as uncut unless its size matches exactly.

(d) Tests:
- Total pieces = sum over cells of cellPieceCount.
- Sum of piece areas plus joint area = finished area.
- Fine pieces with a matching material: needsCut false. Without one: needsCut true.
- PDF counts = stats counts.
- Progress with k=4 (16 pieces) round-trips through serialize.

STAGE 2 (L, after Stage 1): zones with their own grid, as the auditor proposed, for pitch ratios that are not whole numbers (e.g. 10/1 base with 5/1 fine). Required conditions:
- The zone covers whole base cells [c0,c1)×[r0,r1). Lx = colX[c1−1]+colW[c1−1]−colX[c0].
- Inner layout = computeLayout(Lx, Ly, w2, h2, g2, 'cut-both'). Border pieces are computed cuts, so the gap to the neighbouring base stones is exactly g.
- If computeAxis falls back (rest > 0), refuse the zone and show the remainder; never stretch.
- Offer snapping to n-cell multiples for an exact fit (see exactfit.out, e.g. 8/1 with 4/1 needs n=5).
- Covered base cells get CellKind.ZONE with 0 pieces.
- Each zone has its own MosaicData (so its own 16-bit progress per inner cell), uses the project palette as fixedPalette, and gets IDs 'Z1:A001' plus absolute X/Y.
- computeSections must not cut through a zone. A zone larger than a section goes into one section, with a warning.
- Viewer hit-testing, StoneDialog, neighbors, stats, PDF, CSV and serialize all go through the zones first.
- Invariant tests: base pieces + zone pieces = total, no stone counted twice, area plus joints = finished area, measured zone-border gap = g, and PDF sheet == preview for a sheet containing a zone.

findings.title: Section boundaries are placed blindly and run straight through the face; there is no way to move them
findings.problem: Requirement 10's sections fit exactly, but splitAxis spaces the boundaries evenly by length only. In the default portrait, the A1/A2/B1/B2 cross sits in the middle of the face, with the vertical boundary running down the nose. When working with sections on mesh or paper, a seam through the eyes or mouth is the most visible place for a misalignment. The user cannot drag or nudge a boundary.
findings.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/shots/b1-plan.png: the portrait sample (40×50 cm) with 30×30 cm sections puts both boundaries across the face. src/core/layout.ts:233-258 (splitAxis) and evenStarts use only pos/size arrays, with no image, region or detail input.
findings.proposal: Add a seam optimiser in layout.ts. For each axis, take candidate split indices within ±15 % of the even positions. Cost per candidate grid line = Σ over its cells of (100 if in a face region) + detail-map value + the ΔE between neighbouring stones across the joint. Choose the lowest-cost combination where every span still satisfies the size limit (dynamic programming over indices). Boundaries stay on grid lines, so the exact fit and joining marks are unchanged. In the Plan view, add draggable boundary lines that snap to grid lines and are validated live against the maximum section size. Store the indices as settings.sectionColStarts and sectionRowStarts so the PDF uses the same ones.
corrected:
1) Manual boundary control first (main value).
- Add `sectionColCutsMm?: number[]` and `sectionRowCutsMm?: number[]` to ProjectSettings (types.ts). Store millimetres, not indices, so the values survive changes to tile size or joint.
- Add a `sectionMode` value 'manual'. In `sectionsFor` (layout.ts), snap each stored mm value to the nearest grid line with `indexAt` on colX/rowY. Remove duplicates and sort, then call the existing `buildSections`. Boundaries stay on grid lines, so the exact fit and joining marks do not change.
- In StepPlan.tsx, add "Grenzen anpassen". It starts from the current auto starts. Each boundary gets a nudge control of ±1 row/column (and the mm value can be typed). Boundaries are also draggable in Viewer.tsx and snap to grid lines.
- Show each section's real size live. Any section larger than the max size is marked in red, but the user may still save it. Show the actual size rather than refusing.
- Add a "Zurücksetzen (automatisch)" button.
- The worker already calls `sectionsFor(layout, settings)`, so the PDF picks up the same boundaries once the new fields are added to the memo dependencies in useProject.ts:217 and :272.
- Progress needs no migration, because finished sections are derived from per-stone bits.

2) Optional "Gesichter/Details meiden" in automatic mode.
- For each axis, keep the greedy section count k. Search split indices over the whole allowed range (every span at most the max size), not ±15%.
- Add a minimum span, for example max(0.5 × maxLen, the even span − 25%), so narrow leftover strips do not appear.
- Cost per grid line: 100 × the number of cells on that line inside user-drawn face Regions, plus 10 × the number of non-FULL or recommended cells next to the line. The data comes from MosaicData.kind and `regionMask` on the stored regions. Do not use the ΔE between stones across the line as a cost.
- Choose the lowest total with a small dynamic programme over indices, and break ties toward the even split.
- If no candidate improves on the even split, keep the even split.
- Show a hint such as "Grenze verschoben, um Gesicht nicht zu teilen". Never claim the face is avoided when the size limits make that impossible: in the portrait sample at 30x30 cm, every allowed row seam crosses the face region.
- Add a test: the boundaries chosen by the optimiser still give identical stone totals per section, and every section stays within the max size.

1) Types and core
- types.ts: in ProjectSettings and SectionSettings (layout.ts:312), add `sectionMode: 'size' | 'count' | 'custom'`, `sectionColStarts?: number[]`, `sectionRowStarts?: number[]` and `sectionGridKey?: string`. The grid key is `${layout.cols}x${layout.rows}`.
- layout.ts: add `computeSectionsCustom(layout, colStarts, rowStarts)`. It must validate that the starts are strictly increasing, that the first is 0 and that the last is below n. It then calls the existing `buildSections`.
- `sectionsFor`: use the stored starts only if mode is 'custom', `sectionGridKey` matches the current layout, and every span is at most the max section size when that is set. Otherwise fall back to the current size/count split and return a flag such as `customInvalid: true`. The UI then shows a notice like "Abschnittsgrenzen wurden zurückgesetzt, weil sich Größe/Steine/Fuge geändert haben". Never re-optimise silently.
- Extend the worker protocol (protocol.ts:60 `sections: SectionSettings`, and the 'pdf' `msg.settings`) so the PDF, the CSV and the UI all use the same starts.

2) Manual editing in StepPlan.tsx / Viewer.tsx
- Add a "Grenzen anpassen" toggle. It must not be active together with Verlegemodus, so taps are never ambiguous.
- While it is on, section lines in the Viewer can be dragged and snap to the nearest grid line, using `indexAt` on the joint midpoint.
- For phones, also offer per-boundary ±1 Reihe/Spalte nudge buttons.
- Show a live readout of each section's real size in cm and stone count. Refuse or highlight any span over the max size.
- Add a "Gleichmäßig zurücksetzen" button.

3) Optional "Grenzen vorschlagen" button
This runs only on click. The user reviews the result in the preview and then applies it, which stores it as 'custom' starts. It is never recomputed after stone edits.
- Search the full range allowed by the max size. Use exact DP over grid indices per axis with section count k (minimum k from the greedy split), not a ±15 % window. Add a minimum section size (for example at least 40 % of the max) so no thin strips appear.
- Cost per grid line = 10 × number of cells along it inside user-defined face/detail regions (the stored Region list) + 3 × cells where kind ≠ FULL on either side (cut pieces are harder to align across a sheet edge) + a small penalty for moving away from the even position. No ΔE term.
- If every allowed line crosses a face region, as the horizontal seam does in the portrait sample, say so honestly. For example: "Gesicht kann bei max. 30 cm Abschnitt nicht umgangen werden – Abschnittsgröße erhöhen oder Grenze manuell setzen". Do not pretend it has been solved.

4) Tests
- Custom starts produce sections whose stone totals equal the overall stats.
- An invalid or stale grid key falls back to the auto split.
- The PDF and CSV use the same `colStarts` as the UI.
- The suggestion on the portrait sample moves the vertical seam to around 300 mm, with 0 face cells.

findings.title: Grout colour dominates how the finished mosaic looks, but colour matching ignores it (the default light grout washes out every photo)
findings.problem: computeMosaic matches each stone to the photo as if stones covered 100 % of the surface. With 5 mm stones and a 1 mm joint the grout covers 30.6 % of the area (8 mm/1 mm: 21 %). From a normal viewing distance the eye mixes stones and grout in linear light, so the default grout #BDB8AE (src/core/types.ts:212) lifts every dark area (suit, hair, pupils) and desaturates skin. The diagnostics shown on the compute step (StepCompute.tsx:90-94, fed by track() in mosaic.ts) compare only the stone colour with the cell mean. They report 'ΔE ≈ 1.6–3.5', which hides the problem.
findings.evidence: Script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/exp-grout.ts, output in .../algo-quality/out/results/exp-grout.txt. Perceived ΔE00 = Gaussian blur over the full render including grout, σ = 2 pitches, linear light, compared with the blurred photo. Default grout #BDB8AE: obama 40 cm/5 mm 12.8 mean / 29.4 p95; astronaut 10.8/30.0; coffee 12.7/24.8; synthetic portrait sample 11.5/23.9. Same stones with grout #404040: 6.0/8.5, 6.7/9.1, 6.1/7.9, 5.7/8.1. Prototype .../algo-quality/exp-grout-comp.ts (output .../out/results/exp-grout-comp.txt): stone target t' = (t − (1−f)·g)/f in linear RGB, then k-means and matching. Dark grout plus full compensation reaches 2.0/5.1 (obama), 2.7/7.2 (astronaut), 2.3/5.6 (coffee). With the light default grout, compensation cannot help (11.5/28.8) because the darks are out of reach. Visual: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/algo-quality/out/grout-distance-view.png (source | app default | dark grout | dark grout + compensation, downscaled to simulate distance). Photos: public-domain NASA/US-gov portraits and CC0 skimage samples in .../algo-quality/dl/photos/.
findings.proposal: (1) S – Recommend a grout colour. Evaluate a short list of real grout colours (white, light grey, beige, mid grey, anthracite, black) on the downsampled working image in linear light, with stone coverage f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+g)(tileH+g)) from the layout. Preselect the colour with the lowest perceived ΔE and show that number in the joint step (StepGeometry). (2) M – Optional grout-aware colour targets in computeMosaic. Before k-means and matching, convert each cell/piece target to linear RGB and apply t' = clamp((t − (1−f_s)·g)/f_s), where f_s = 1 − s·(1−f) and s is a 'Fernwirkung' strength slider (0–100 %, default 50 %). Match by ΔE00(t', palette). The stone dialog keeps showing the original photo colour, so nothing is hidden. (3) S – Add an honest 'Fernwirkung ΔE' diagnostic (blur including grout) next to the existing ΔE. Expected: perceived mean ΔE about −50 % from the grout choice alone and about −80 % with compensation on real photos.
corrected:
1) (S) Grout recommendation in StepGeometry. Candidates: white #F2F0EA, the light grey #BDB8AE, beige, mid grey #808080, anthracite #404040 and black #202020.
- Compute it on the working image, downsampled to about one pixel per cell. For each candidate g, take the mean and p95 of ΔE00(f·t + (1−f)·g, t) in linear RGB, where t is the photo colour and f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+joint)(tileH+joint)).
- Show the best candidate with its ΔE next to the grout colour picker, plus a one-click 'Übernehmen' button.
- Never override the user's chosen or default grout on its own.
- Recompute when tile size, joint width or image changes.

2) (S) Honest distance preview.
- In buildOverviewRGBA (src/core/render.ts:93), blend each cell's colour with the grout colour in linear light, using that cell's coverage f_cell. Then the zoomed-out view (render.ts:165) shows the real effect instead of stone colours only.
- Optionally add a 'Fernwirkung' toggle in the Viewer that renders the whole mosaic this way at any zoom level.

3) (S) Distance diagnostic in StepCompute. Add a second row, 'Farbabweichung aus Entfernung inkl. Fuge (Schätzung)': mean and p95 ΔE00 of f_cell·stone + (1−f_cell)·grout against the photo cell, computed in linear light. f_cell = (sum of the cell's piece polygon areas from cellPieces/subRects) / ((colW+joint)·(rowH+joint)). Label it as an estimate and state its assumption: the joints blend into the stones at viewing distance.

4) (M, optional, default OFF) Grout-aware colour targets in computeMosaic.
- Add a 'Fugenkompensation' slider (0–100 %, default 0).
- Before k-means and matching, give each piece a target t' = clamp((t_lin − (1−f_s)·g_lin)/f_s, 0, 1), with f_s = 1 − s·(1 − f_cell).
- Use the per-cell coverage, not a single layout-wide f. Subdivided cells reach about 44–60 % coverage, against 69–79 % for whole stones.
- Store s in the project settings and show it in the PDF and legend.
- The stone dialog keeps the original photo colour, the chosen stone colour and both ΔE values.
- Add tests: with s=0 the output is identical to today; with s>0 the distance ΔE drops on the sample images and nothing else changes (counts, geometry, cut dimensions).

(1) S/M, do this first: a grout recommendation instead of silently preselecting a colour.
- Add the function `recommendGrout(img, layout, candidates)` in a new src/core/grout.ts.
- Candidates are generic named colours, not brands: Weiß #F2F0EA, Hellgrau/Beige #BDB8AE, Silbergrau #9A9A96, Zementgrau #808080, Dunkelgrau #5A5A5A, Anthrazit #404040, Schwarz #202020, plus the user's current groutHex.
- Model it analytically on the cell grid, so no rasterisation is needed and it scales to millions of stones in 64-cell tiles. For each cell take the linear-RGB cell mean t. Before compute, use the photo; after compute, use the assigned stone colour. Perceived colour = f·t + (1−f)·g, with f = tileW·tileH/((tileW+joint)(tileH+joint)) from the layout. Apply a Gaussian blur over cells with σ = 2 cells, convert to Lab, and take ΔE00 against the blurred photo.
- In StepGeometry, next to the grout colour picker, show 'Empfehlung: Dunkelgrau – Fernwirkung ΔE ≈ 6 (aktuell 12,8)' with an 'Übernehmen' button. Never overwrite the user's choice or their Settings default automatically.
- Label it as an estimate. Add a note that real grout dries lighter and differs between brands, so the user should enter the HEX of a dried sample.
- Optionally, change the factory default (types.ts:212, db.ts:124) from #BDB8AE to #808080. That halves far-view ΔE in every case tested.

(2) S: honest diagnostics in StepCompute.
- Rename the existing value to 'ΔE Stein ↔ Foto (Nahansicht)'.
- Add 'Fernwirkung inkl. Fuge (Modell-Schätzung)', computed with the same cell-grid model in the worker after compute (mosaic.ts diagnostics, or a separate worker message).
- Recompute it when the grout changes without recomputing the mosaic, because only the grout term changes.

(3) M, optional and OFF by default: grout-aware colour targets.
- Add `groutCompensation` (0–100 %, default 0) and pass `groutLin` and `f` into ComputeParams.
- Before k-means sampling and before matching (mosaic.ts:417-541), map each cell/piece target t to t' = (t − (1−f_s)·g)/f_s in linear RGB, with f_s = 1 − s_eff·(1−f).
- Compute s_eff per stone and channel as min(s, t/(g(1−f)), (1−t)/((1−f)(1−g))), so targets never clip. Plain clamping crushed shadow detail in testing.
- Add groutHex and s to computeKey (useProject.ts:18) only when s > 0, so grout changes stay preview-only when compensation is off.
- Show a hint when the grout is lighter than the median image L*: 'Kompensation hilft bei heller Fuge kaum – dunklere Fuge wählen'.
- Add the original photo colour and its ΔE to StoneDialog. It is not shown there today.
- Tests:
  - stone and colour totals stay identical to the assignment counts;
  - with s = 0 the result is bit-identical to the current behaviour;
  - with dark grout and s = 50 %, far ΔE goes down and near ΔE stays at or below about 4.5 on the sample portrait.

findings.title: APK file saving gives no feedback and fails silently on Android 10; after the share sheet the user cannot find or reopen the PDF/CSV/backup
findings.problem: saveNative (platform.ts:20-36) tries Directory.Documents and silently swallows any failure. It returns savedPath, but downloadBlob ignores it (components.tsx:157-160). Callers do not await it (StepPdf.tsx:73, StepPlan.tsx:48, Projects.tsx:76), so errors become unhandled rejections. On native the 'Öffnen' link is hidden (StepPdf.tsx:182), and the only message is 'PDF erstellt (x KB).' The Filesystem plugin's own README says Directory.Documents on Android 10 and older needs READ+WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. The manifest declares only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdkVersion=28, no READ, and no requestLegacyExternalStorage, so on Android 10 (API 29) the Documents write is rejected and only the share sheet remains. If the user dismisses it, the file exists only in the app cache. This matters especially for project export, which README names as the only protection against data loss when reinstalling.
findings.evidence: Code: src/platform.ts:22-27 (try writeFile Documents, catch {}), src/ui/components.tsx:158-160 ('await saveNative(blob, name); return;' with the result unused), android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (only WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion=28), node_modules/@capacitor/filesystem/README.md lines 114-123 ('in Android 10 and older, this API requires ... READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE ... WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE'), and FilesystemPlugin.kt:408-416 (below API 30 it requires the PUBLIC_STORAGE alias = READ+WRITE). The i18n string 'pdfui.done' (de.ts:402) gives no location. Not testable on a device here; the conclusion comes from the plugin source and docs.
findings.proposal: 1) Make downloadBlob return {savedPath, shared, error} and await it everywhere. findings.title: Android edge-to-edge: dark status-bar icons over the dark top bar, and modals and page bottom ignore safe areas
findings.problem: With targetSdk 36, viewport-fit=cover (index.html) and Capacitor 8's SystemBars plugin, a WebView of version 140 or newer receives real insets (SystemBars.java:194). The app's navy top bar (#1d2a3a, styles.css:81-92, padding-top env(safe-area-inset-top)) is then drawn behind the status bar. No SystemBars style is configured (capacitor.config.ts), so the DEFAULT style resolves to LIGHT in light mode (SystemBars.java:327-333), which means dark status-bar icons on the dark bar. In system dark mode the navigation bar gets light icons over the light page background. Modals do not use safe-area insets (.modal-backdrop padding 12px, .modal max-height 92vh), and main padding-bottom is a fixed 40px.
findings.evidence: Code: SystemBars.java:39 (WEBVIEW_VERSION_WITH_SAFE_AREA_FIX = 140), :194 (passthrough when WebView >= 140 && viewport-fit=cover), :292 (setAppearanceLightStatusBars(!DARK)), :327 getStyleForTheme(). core-plugins.d.ts:242-262 (Light = 'dark system bar content'). Simulation with CDP Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride (top 40, bottom 48): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/ux-mobile-android/scripts/safearea.cjs (output .../out/safearea.txt): 'modal top 34 bottom 810 | status bar ends at 40, nav bar starts at 796'. Screenshot .../shots/m-safearea.png shows the modal top under the status bar and the modal bottom under the navigation bar. The icon colour cannot be verified without a device; it follows from the plugin source.
findings.proposal: In main.tsx, when isNative(): import { SystemBars, SystemBarsStyle, SystemBarType } from '@capacitor/core'; call SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Dark, bar: SystemBarType.StatusBar }) and SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Light, bar: SystemBarType.NavigationBar }). In capacitor.config.ts add plugins: { SystemBars: { initialViewportFitValueHint: 'cover' } } to avoid layout jumps. CSS: .modal-backdrop { padding: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-top)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-right)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left)) }, .modal { max-height: calc(100dvh - env(safe-area-inset-top) - env(safe-area-inset-bottom) - 24px) }, main { padding-bottom: calc(40px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) }, and the sticky step bar (separate finding) also uses env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
corrected:
1) src/main.tsx: only when isNative() and the insets really reach the page, call `import { SystemBars, SystemBarsStyle, SystemBarType } from '@capacitor/core'` (all exported in @capacitor/core 8.6.0, dist/index.js:647). To check that the insets reach the page, add a probe element with `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` and read it with getComputedStyle. Read it again on `resize`, or for about 1 s after load, because the plugin calls requestApplyInsets only after onPageCommitVisible. If the probe height is above 0, call `SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Dark, bar: SystemBarType.StatusBar })` for light icons over the navy .topbar. Then call `SystemBars.setStyle({ style: SystemBarsStyle.Light, bar: SystemBarType.NavigationBar })` for dark icons over the light #f4f1ec page. If the probe is 0, keep DEFAULT. In that case the plugin pads the decor view and the bars sit over the theme's window background, which DEFAULT already handles. The plugin re-applies the explicit style when the configuration changes (SystemBars.java:109-114), so one call is enough.

2) capacitor.config.ts: add `plugins: { SystemBars: { initialViewportFitValueHint: 'cover' } }` so the first layout gets the insets without a jump. Then run `npx cap sync`.

3) src/ui/styles.css:
- `.modal-backdrop`: set `padding: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-top)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-right)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left))`.
- `.modal`: replace `max-height: 92vh` with `max-height: 100%`. The backdrop is position:fixed with inset 0, so 100% is its content height once the padding is subtracted.
- `main`: set `padding-bottom: calc(40px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`.
- Optional: change `.topbar` `padding-top` to `calc(8px + env(safe-area-inset-top))`, so the bar's content does not sit right against the status bar.

4) Check it on a real Android 15 or 16 phone with current WebView, in light and dark mode, with both gesture and 3-button navigation. Also test with the --safe-area-inset-top=0 path, by setting the SystemBars config `insetsHandling: 'native'`.

Impact 3 and effort S stand. The status-bar icon contrast is the part the user will notice. The modal and page-bottom changes are small polish: an overlap of 6-18px, and only with 3-button navigation.

findings.title: Automatic face (and eye) detection never works in practice; face protection depends on the user drawing ellipses
findings.problem: Requirements 5 and 6 (auto-suggest finer stones in faces and eyes; faces must not be distorted) rely on the FaceDetector Shape Detection API. That API is not enabled in standard Chromium, and the APK's WebView is Chromium-based. For a user's own photo the app therefore has no face region by default. Only the generic skin-tone weighting and the edge-density detail map apply. Eyes, mouth and other features are not detected at all.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/spec-gaps/b1.cjs output: 'FaceDetector in window: false'. After clicking 'Gesichter erkennen' the UI says 'Automatische Gesichtserkennung wird von diesem Browser nicht unterstützt – bitte Gesichtsbereich manuell markieren.' (shots/b1-shapes.png). src/ui/project/imagePrep.ts:153-163 is the only detection path and returns null without the API. The sample portrait has a face region only because it is hard-coded in src/ui/Home.tsx (SAMPLES).
findings.proposal: Bundle an offline detector that runs in the compute worker. For example pico.js (MIT; about 2 KB of code plus a ~240 KB cascade) with its 'puploc' pupil localiser, or MediaPipe BlazeFace short-range (Apache-2.0) if the WASM size is acceptable. Precache it with Workbox so it works offline. Turn the detections into suggested Regions: a face ellipse and two eye ellipses, labelled 'automatisch erkannt – bitte prüfen' with their confidence. The user confirms or drags them; nothing is applied without visible regions. In eye regions, apply the finest option available (a zone from the mixed-size finding, or SUB), and lower λ so pupils and highlights are not averaged away. Add a test that checks the sample portrait gets a face box overlapping the hard-coded one.
corrected:

2. Eyes.
   - Only add pico's puploc localiser (about 1.2 MB) if its licence is confirmed.
   - Otherwise add one 'detail' region (existing type, already λ×0.5 and subdivision allowed in mosaic.ts) covering the eye band. Place it at fixed proportions of the detected face box, e.g. y = box.y + 0.25…0.5·h, x = box.x + 0.1…0.9·w.
   - Label it 'geschätzt' (estimated), not 'erkannt' (detected).

3. UX in StepPhoto / StepShapes.
   - Run detection automatically after the photo is loaded or cropped, mapping coordinates into crop space and rerunning when the crop changes. This way the step-1 background-simplify preview (StepPhoto.tsx:50 passes rec.regions) already protects the face.
   - Add the results as suggested regions with a `source: 'auto'` flag and the confidence. Draw them dashed, listed as 'automatisch erkannt – bitte prüfen (Konfidenz x)', each with the existing delete button.
   - Add move/resize handles for regions; today regions can only be drawn and deleted.
   - With zero detections, show the existing 'faceNone' / manual-marking hint. Never apply anything silently.

4. Tests.
   - Add a small public-domain real portrait (e.g. a US-government official portrait) as tests/fixtures. Assert that one face is found whose box centre lies inside a hand-annotated face box.
   - Assert that the landscape and city samples yield no detection above the score threshold.
   - Do not rely on the synthetic cartoon sample. Keep its hard-coded region.

5. Update README.md:147 to describe the bundled detector, its frontal-face limitation and that suggestions must be confirmed.

Effort: M.

1) Detector: vendor pico.js (MIT, 5.6 KB) and the facefinder cascade (~240 KB) under src/vendor/pico/, wrapped in a typed module, plus lploc.js and puploc.bin (~1.2 MB) as an optional second stage. Load them lazily with a dynamic import or fetch the first time detection runs, and make sure the globPatterns in vite.config.ts include the .bin files (add 'bin') so it works offline and in the APK. On the 640 px canvas that RegionEditor already renders, run on the main thread or in compute.worker.ts through a new 'detectFaces' message in protocol.ts. Keep FaceDetector as the first choice where it exists. Use a quality threshold (pico demo: q > 50) and cluster_detections. Return {box, q, pupils?}.

2) Suggestions, not results: add optional fields to Region in types.ts: source: 'auto' | 'manual' and confidence?: number (serialize.ts/db.ts must accept old records). Show auto regions with a dashed outline and the label 'automatisch erkannt – bitte prüfen (Sicherheit 87 %)'. Offer 'Übernehmen' and 'Verwerfen' buttons. Add move and resize handles to RegionEditor in StepShapes.tsx, so a misplaced ellipse can be fixed and does not have to be deleted and redrawn. Keep the existing box expansion (StepShapes.tsx:121). Run detection once automatically after a photo is uploaded. If it finds something, show a hint in the Shapes and Compute steps ('1 Gesicht erkannt – Bereich prüfen'). Nothing is applied silently.

3) Make eye regions actually do something: add Region.type 'eye', or make 'detail' nest. In mosaic.ts:229-233, replace the else-if with multiplicative factors: lambda *= (inFace ? 0.4 : 1) * (inDetailOrEye ? 0.5 : 1). In eye regions also set weight[idx] *= 2 so k-means keeps pupil and highlight colours. Do not bypass pieceCuttable/minPieceMm: piece validity and cut dimensions stay computed geometrically. Once mixed tile sizes exist, eye regions can also pick the smallest zone tile.

4) Honest scope: the i18n strings (de/en/tr) and README.md:147 should say that only frontal human faces are detected, not profiles or animals. Manual marking stays available.

5) Tests: add a vitest that runs the detector on a small committed public-domain real-photo fixture and asserts IoU > 0.3 with a hand-labelled box. Add one that asserts no detection above the threshold on landscape.png and city.png. Add one that asserts the synthetic portrait does not crash. Add a core test that an 'eye' region inside a face changes λ, i.e. more non-FULL cells than face alone, while the stats and count invariants still hold.

Impact 3-4: measured face ΔE 4.31→3.83 and twice as many cuts in the face once a region exists. Effort M.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
